newsitem.title: USA: Third pipeline project for Sable gas to be filed.
newsitem.headline: Third pipeline project for Sable gas to be filed.

text.p: Houston-based Tatham Offshore Inc expects to file with Canadian regulators within 30 days its proposal for an underwater pipeline to carry Atlantic natural gas to New England, a company official said on Monday.

It is the third pipeline proposed to carry natural gas to the United States from the planned Sable Island fields off Nova Scotia. The others, Maritimes & Northeast and Trans-Quebec & Maritimes, both want to use land routes.

Tatham's proposal has advantages over its rivals because it could also carry gas from fields that may be developed on the Grand Banks of the Atlantic Ocean off Newfoundland, said company vice-president Dennis Kunetka.
"It would be a solution for the entire eastern Canadian coast and not just for the Sable Island project," Kunetka said. "We think it's a better solution."

The 2,200 km (1,367 mile) pipeline would make landfall in the United States at Seabrook, New Hampshire and cost "in the neighborhood of US$3 billion" to construct, Kunetka said in a telephone interview.

The company expects to file its proposal with Canada's National Energy Board within 30 days. It has already asked an NEB-led panel reviewing the Maritimes & Northeast pipeline to delay a decision on that project.

Maritimes & Northeast spokesman Michael Whalen said it would be "entirely inappropriate" for Canadian regulators to delay a decision on its project. The NEB panel was expected to render its decision in September.

Whalen said the Maritimes & Northeast proposal had "obvious advantages" over Tatham's because a land route to the Boston area would also service markets in Nova Scotia, New Brunswick and Maine that do have access to natural gas.
Like Maritimes & Northeast, the Trans-Quebec & Maritimes (TQM) pipeline was designed to deliver natural gas to the Boston area but along a route that would extend to Montreal before heading south.
Maritimes & Northeast is owned by Mobil Corp, Westcoast Energy Inc and Duke Energy Corp unit PanEnergy. Mobil Corp unit Mobil Oil Canada is Sable Island's lead developer.
TQM is co-owned by TransCanada PipeLines Ltd and Gaz Metropolitain and Co LP. IPL Energy Inc recently joined the TQM project.
Development costs for both projects were estimated at C$1 billion ($730 million) each.
